title: Original face
hook: what was your face before your parents were born (Gateless Gate 23)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Mahakassapa, who smiled at the flower, and your line, the smile.

Count your faces. The one in your passport photo. The one on video calls, slightly brighter than real life. The face for your boss, the face for your oldest friend, the face you make at a baby. The one in the mirror at six in the morning, before you've decided who to be today. Which one is really you? Zen has a question that goes further back than any of them, and it comes from a chase through the mountains. What was your face before your parents were born?
screen: `THE PASSPORT FACE. THE VIDEO-CALL FACE.` → `THE SIX A.M. MIRROR.` → `WHICH ONE IS YOU?`

segments.voice: Remember Huineng from two days ago, the poor man from the south who received the Fifth Patriarch's robe and bowl. The Gateless Gate, in case twenty-three, tells what happened next. Huineng fled south with the robe, and some monks, furious that an outsider had it, chased him. The first to reach him, the story says, was a monk named Ming, once an army officer. He caught up with Huineng in the mountains. Huineng set the robe and bowl on a rock and said: this robe stands for faith; can it be taken by force? Take it. Ming tried to lift it. It wouldn't move, as if it were a mountain. Shaking, Ming said: I came for the teaching, not the robe. Please teach me. Huineng said: don't think good, don't think bad. Right now, at this very moment, what is your original face? Ming woke up on the spot. He had come full of opinions: who deserved the robe, who was right, who was wrong. Huineng asks him to drop all of that and look at what's here before any of the labels. Later Zen teachers put the same question another way, the version in today's title: what was your face before your father and mother were born? It isn't about biology or past lives. It points at what you are before all the faces you've learned to wear, before good and bad, before your name. Teachers don't explain the answer. Like mu, like the flag, it's held and looked into until it looks back.
screen: `A CHASE THROUGH THE MOUNTAINS.` · `THE ROBE WOULDN'T MOVE.` · `DON'T THINK GOOD, DON'T THINK BAD.` · `BEFORE YOUR PARENTS WERE BORN.` · then, large: `BEFORE YOU WERE BORN.`

segments.voice: If there's a mirror near you, look into it quietly; if not, close your eyes and feel your face from the inside, and let the expression you're wearing soften. Let the judgments that come, tired, older, fine, pass without arguing. Then ask gently, without looking for an answer: what was my face before my parents were born?
Original face. What you are before good and bad, before every face you learned to wear: Huineng's question to Ming in the mountains.
Your line: before you were born. Under every face, the one you never had to learn. Day two hundred eighty-four, done.

howItsDone: In Rinzai Zen 'original face' is often given as an early koan; students hold the question in sitting and daily life and bring their response to private interviews with the teacher.

original.note: Chinese běnlái miànmù: original face, literally 'the face as it was from the start'.

trapdoor: what you thought: 'original face' means what you looked like as a baby.
what it means: what you are before every learned face, before good and bad.
what a scholar hears: the Gateless Gate's wording is 'not thinking good, not thinking evil'; the 'before your parents were born' form is a later Zen phrasing of the same koan.

sources.ref: Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch, Huineng and Huiming

notes: Case 23 paraphrased. The index hook says 'before your parents were born'; Gateless Gate 23 itself has 'not thinking good, not thinking evil… what is your original face'. The script teaches both and says which is which.
Ming (Huiming) as a former army officer (general): traditional detail, confirm.
Original 本來面目 and pronunciation: confirm.
